version_findings.precise_disparity_statement: ATB arXiv v1 section4.2 qualitative synthetic discussion. Supports external precise geometry for the synthetic baseline group, not an exact private adapter specification.
version_findings.builtin_depth_statement: ATB arXiv v1 AppendixD describes DeepLens real-world examples using its built-in depth model. The statement is absent from the reviewed v2/final wording; do not generalize it into a verified current full DAVIS protocol.
version_findings.LPIPS: Official ICLR2026 proceedings PDF Table1 includes LPIPS. arXiv v2 Table1 and the existing repository PDF omit the column. Prior unqualified not-reported claims are corrected; frozen six-metric selection histories are not retrospectively changed.

derivation.measured_model: R_eff approximately c*aperture*abs(D-Df), fixed native single-SR/output resolution
derivation.raw_disparity_equivalent: Without another minmax transform: aperture=K/c. Unsaturated signed inputs are algebraically identical after affine compensation.
derivation.warning: K/c applied after per-frame minmax increases effective raw-disparity blur scale by1/s. Compensation is a fixed unit conversion, not per-scene score tuning.
derivation.limits: c is an empirical edge-width coefficient, not the physical training aperture or a strict kernel support bound; saturation breaks exact raw/normalized equivalence.

calibration_scope: Existing32controls measure the LensBlur/SR operator after canonical geometry inputs. They do not minmax a constant-depth image. A complete adapter must explicitly reject zero span or use a predeclared separate case, not silently divide by zero. Avoid colocating a depth discontinuity with the measured RGB edge when estimating single-plane blur width.
limits: K/32 has no verified author-adapter evidence and does not match this measured single-SR edge response.
No change to dataset, predictions, evaluation metrics, checkpoints, Dr.Bokeh geometry/gamma, or main-table adapter selection.
Geometry statistics use only saved input min/max values, never prediction scores. Required-aperture ranges are descriptive estimates under the not-yet-frozen linear fit.
LPIPS paper references are now available; the current project implementation remains lpips squeeze v0.1. Public code also names squeeze, but no new numerical-parity claim is made.
